source.title: Scaling View Synthesis Transformers
source.authors: Evan Kim; Hyunwoo Ryu; Thomas W. Mitchel; Vincent Sitzmann

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures scaling in view-synthesis transformers and reports settings where scaling does and does not hold, including a multiview failure that is remedied by relative camera attention.
record.gate_note: The study tests scaling of vision/view-synthesis models, not language-model pretraining loss. Its primary metric is test LPIPS. It fits LPIPS-versus-compute and model/data-versus-compute trends, and reports multiview and fixed-latent exceptions. It does not test language-model token allocation, downstream-task predictability, or architecture details at fixed parameter count.
record.test_reason: The study fits LPIPS-versus-compute Pareto frontiers and Chinchilla-style N_opt/D_opt power laws for view-synthesis transformers, a new setting. Its own results show where the power-law form holds (stereo; multiview with PRoPE), where it breaks (multiview without PRoPE) and where it weakens (fixed latent). That makes it T3 rather than T5; it does not argue that the LM versions are wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the following. SVSM matches LVSM's scaling slope while needing 2–3x less training compute. The SVSM compute-optimal split is roughly equal in N and D, as in Chinchilla. The scaling-law-chosen models set a new state of the art. Relative camera pose embeddings are key to multiview scaling. Fixed-latent designs scale substantially worse.
record.recipe_differences: Applies scaling analysis to view-synthesis transformers and test LPIPS rather than language-model pretraining loss and tokens; studies model size and data samples, with view-count, architecture, pose-attention, and latent-bottleneck choices.
record.method_sensitivity: Scaling varies with model family, loss range, view-count regime, relative camera attention (PRoPE), and whether the scene representation has a fixed-size latent bottleneck.

fits_no_version.finding: Effective batch size hypothesis. Runs with the same B·V_T give the same training loss and test PSNR (variation at most ±0.1–0.2 PSNR) across models, datasets and view counts (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In NVS training, scenes per batch times target views per scene acts as the true batch size.

record.peer_reviewed: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (venue stated in supplied metadata)
record.problems: The authors say the frontier trend is not perfectly linear and fit separate LPIPS ranges. They note the LVSM compute-optimal fit does not hold exactly. Some scaling outcomes are shown only in figures; no statistical uncertainty for the fitted coefficients is reported. The compute-optimal data includes repeated scene samples, and the authors note their datasets are small.
record.rows_left_out: Left out Table 1 and Table 4 reconstruction metrics not needed to record the scaling-law result beyond the scaling-recipe model rows R9–R10; also left out Table 2 comparisons to geometry-aware methods and Table 10 PRoPE ablation metrics, which do not directly measure the claimed scaling relations.

untested.parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss versus N, D or C.
Extrapolation of loss by orders of magnitude. Only about 8–10x beyond the sweep, with no numeric predicted-versus-observed loss.
LM parameter/token allocation. The NVS analogue is recorded under V5/V7.
No controlled depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count. The encoder/decoder split is explicitly not studied.
Video, image generation, fine-tuning, transfer. Repeated-data effects are not isolated.

missing.what: Bottleneck-free scaling on Objaverse V_C=8: SVSM and LVSM decoder-only scale equally, with SVSM's frontier shifted 5x on compute.
Compute range of the stereo sweeps: 100 petaflops to 100 exaflops (~3 orders of magnitude), models ~7M–300M parameters.
Compiled frontiers across RE10K, DL3DV and Objaverse.

record.verdict_notes: Changed T5 to T3. The record's uncertainty_reported='y' is wrong: no confidence intervals are given for any fitted coefficient. Rows R9 and R10 are largely comparisons of the study's own method with others. The metric is test LPIPS, chosen because it gives near-linear log-log trends; this is not the training loss. The sample counts include repeated data from small datasets.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No language models or extrapolation by orders of magnitude are tested; the reported model-size sweep is around 7M to 300M parameters, with additional larger models trained for comparisons.
The study fits parameter-count and data-sample-count trends for view synthesis, not language-model parameter and token counts under fixed compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architectural details at a fixed parameter count.
Tests view-synthesis transformers and repeated scene data; does not test image/video generation models generally, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream-task performance as a function of pretraining loss or scale.
Shows sensitivity to architecture and multiview pose treatment, and piecewise LPIPS-versus-compute fits; does not vary language-model parameter counting, language-model data, or fitting method.

rows.subject: LVSM
rows.size_stated: model sizes around 7M to 300M parameters in scaling sweeps
rows.operation_detail: Fit test LPIPS versus compute on the Pareto frontier; coefficient for the first loss range.
rows.measure: LPIPS-versus-compute power-law coefficient c in P(χ) ∝ χ^c
rows.note: Authors say the trend is not perfectly linear and fit separate sections of the frontier.
rows.check: For V5, LPIPS falls near-linearly on log-log over the 100 PF–100 EF range. For V7, the frontier bends: slope -0.23 above LPIPS 0.14 versus -0.12 below.

rows.note: The second fitted slope differs from the first.
rows.check: Second-segment slope of -0.12 versus -0.23 shows the curve bending away from a single power law (V7).

rows.subject: SVSM, Pareto-optimal model
rows.operation_detail: Train a larger model using the fitted scaling recipe and report its test result.
rows.note: The paper describes the scaling-law-following SVSM model as outperforming the compared models; this is a reported larger-model result, not an orders-of-magnitude extrapolation test.
rows.check: This is mainly the study's own method compared with LVSM. It bears on V2 only because the recipe was extrapolated about one order of magnitude (sweep max ~1e20 FLOPs; final run ~7.7e20 FLOPs). The scaling-law-chosen 416M model beat the 740M iter-matched model (LPIPS 0.096 vs 0.098). No predicted LPIPS is stated, so there is no predicted-versus-actual loss check. The text calls it SVSM-420M while the table gives 416M. Not V5/V7 evidence.

source_check.correct: Table 1: 416M parameters, 170k iterations, 0.77 zflops, LPIPS 0.096; decoder-only LVSM: 1.60 zflops, LPIPS 0.098. V2 state: cannot_determine. No extrapolated numerical loss prediction is evaluated.
source_check.locator_found: §5, Table 1, final-model discussion and patch-size adjustment footnote
source_check.problem: A successful model-choice comparison cannot establish even partial accuracy of V2's orders-of-magnitude loss prediction.

rows.subject: SVSM Enc-Dec (ours, Pareto-optimal)
rows.operation_detail: Train a multiview model using the fitted Pareto-optimal scaling recipe and report its test result.
rows.note: The authors report that the model following the scaling laws outperforms both listed models; the reported compute and metric are in Table 4.
rows.check: Own method compared with LVSM+PRoPE at a single compute level (44 eflops), which may lie inside the multiview sweep range. There is no predicted value and no extrapolation shown.

rows.subject: SVSM
rows.operation_detail: Measure Pareto-frontier scaling without relative camera attention.
rows.note: Text explicitly says the SVSM frontier saturates much quicker than LVSM as training compute increases.
rows.check: The section is titled 'Scaling Law Does Not Hold': SVSM's multiview frontier saturates much sooner than LVSM's. Scaling depends on pose handling (V7 observed). The value is figure-only.

source_check.correct: The scaling experiment uses VC=4 on DL3DV. Vanilla SVSM initially improves but saturates and stops scaling much earlier than LVSM. V5: partial over the sweep, absent in the saturated regime; V7: observed.
source_check.locator_found: §6, analysis setup and scaling-failure discussion; Fig. 7a
source_check.problem: The single partial state obscures explicitly stopped scaling at higher compute and fully observed setup dependence.

rows.subject: SVSM with PRoPE
rows.operation_detail: Measure Pareto-frontier scaling after adding relative camera attention and retraining.
rows.note: Text says equivalent scaling is re-established and SVSM maintains a tighter Pareto frontier.
rows.check: With PRoPE, 'equivalent scaling is re-established'. The value is figure-only.

rows.subject: SVSM-fixed
rows.operation_detail: Compare compute-performance scaling with a fixed-size scene latent.
rows.measure: Scaling behavior and compute needed for the same performance
rows.baseline: Bottleneck-free SVSM and LVSM decoder-only designs
rows.note: Text says fixed-latent designs scale substantially worse than their bottleneck-free counterparts; SVSM-fixed has a Pareto advantage over LVSM encoder-decoder.
rows.check: Scaling persists but is 'substantially worse' than in bottleneck-free designs. No exponents are given and the result is figure-only. For V7, it shows exponent dependence on the latent design.

source_check.correct: Fixed-latent SVSM scales substantially worse than bottleneck-free designs and retains a compute advantage over LVSM encoder-decoder. V7: observed. V5 functional form: cannot_determine from the qualitative comparison; no fitted exponent is reported.
source_check.problem: Worse scaling alone does not establish a partial failure of the same power-law form.

rows.subject: LVSM Encoder-Decoder
rows.operation_detail: Compare scaling behavior with a fixed-size scene latent.
rows.measure: Scaling behavior versus SVSM-fixed and bottleneck-free designs
rows.baseline: Bottleneck-free SVSM and LVSM decoder-only designs
rows.note: Text says the two fixed-latent designs exhibit similar scaling and both scale substantially worse than bottleneck-free designs.
rows.check: Same as R13. This is a comparator row, figure-only.

source_check.correct: LVSM encoder-decoder and SVSM-fixed exhibit similar scaling, substantially worse than bottleneck-free designs. V7: observed. V5 functional form: cannot_determine from the qualitative comparison; no fitted exponent is reported.
source_check.problem: A qualitative reduction in scaling efficiency does not establish failure of a power-law functional form.

relationships.condition: Stereo NVS on RealEstate10K (LVSM and SVSM); multiview DL3DV with PRoPE; Objaverse bottleneck-free designs
relationships.reason: LPIPS falls near-linearly in log-log over ~3 orders of compute (R1–R4). SVSM N_opt/D_opt follow power laws with a≈b (R7, R8). Scaling returns with PRoPE (R12). The Objaverse support comes from the text and Fig. 9a, not from a row.
relationships.display_finding: LPIPS decreased nearly linearly on log-log axes over approximately three orders of magnitude in compute, while SVSM optimal model and data allocations followed power laws with a≈b and scaling gains returned with PRoPE and appeared in bottleneck-free Objaverse designs.

relationships.reason: The frontier bends, with slope moving from -0.23 to -0.12 (R1–R4). The compute-optimal split differs by architecture, 0.65/0.33 versus 0.52/0.47 (R5–R8). Scaling depends on pose attention and the latent bottleneck (R11–R14).
relationships.display_finding: The frontier slope changed from −0.23 to −0.12, compute-optimal allocation exponents differed by architecture (0.65/0.33 versus 0.52/0.47), and pose attention and the latent bottleneck affected scaling.
